findings.title: Route guard enforces authentication: unauthenticated deep-link bounces to /login (verified)
findings.cvss: N/A (positive finding) — confirms the SPA refuses to render a protected route without a session and preserves the intended destination via ?next=
findings.description: The Playwright test named 'E2E: demo-skip bypass navigates without auth' clicks the first type=button (the ghost 'continue as demo / skip login' control) on the login form and records the resulting URL. The test name expects an auth bypass, but the captured artifact shows the route guard correctly intercepted the navigation: instead of landing on /risk, the browser ended up at /login with the intended destination preserved as a query parameter. The test still reports 'ok' because it only writes the URL to a file (no assertion), but the recorded URL is the real verified outcome and demonstrates the front-end route guard is working as designed.
findings.rootCause: Client-side route guard redirects any navigation toward a protected path to /login?next=<encoded-path> when no valid session token is present, rather than rendering the protected view.
findings.evidence: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/demo-bypass-url.txt contains exactly: 'http://localhost:5173/login?next=%2Frisk' — the ghost button did NOT reach /risk; it was bounced back to /login with next=%2Frisk. playwright.log: 'ok 3 ... E2E: demo-skip bypass navigates without auth (3.0s)'.
findings.impact: Positive: confirms protected routes (e.g. /risk) cannot be reached by clicking the demo/skip control or by direct deep-linking without authentication. The ?next redirect also means UX intent is preserved post-login.
findings.reproduction: 1) Run the live stack (frontend :5173, backend :8084). 2) Open /login. 3) Without entering credentials, click the ghost/skip button (form.login-form button[type=button]). 4) Observe the URL resolves to /login?next=%2Frisk, not /risk. Reproduced by audit.spec.ts:54-61, artifact demo-bypass-url.txt.
findings.resolution: No code fix required for the guard itself. Recommend renaming the test and adding a real assertion (expect(page.url()).toMatch(/\/login/)) so the suite fails loudly if the guard ever regresses; the current test would pass even if the bypass succeeded because it makes no assertion.

findings.title: Happy-path authentication journeys verified: login success, login failure, and session-on-reload
findings.cvss: N/A (positive finding) — three core auth journeys exercised end-to-end against the live app and all pass
findings.description: Three authentication journeys are exercised end-to-end against the running app: (1) valid admin login (admin/Admin@12345) submits the real login form and lands on /risk; (2) invalid login (admin/WrongPassword!1) surfaces a visible .login-error element and stays on /login; (3) after a successful login a full page reload re-renders the authenticated route (/risk) rather than bouncing to /login, proving the session token survives a reload. report.json records expected:6, unexpected:0, flaky:0.
findings.rootCause: N/A — positive verification of intended behavior.
findings.evidence: playwright.log: 'ok 1 ... login success -> lands on /risk (1.7s)', 'ok 2 ... login failure -> error shown, stays on /login (1.7s)', 'ok 4 ... session persists across reload (3.8s)'. reload-url.txt contains exactly 'http://localhost:5173/risk' (still authenticated after reload). report.json stats: expected 6, unexpected 0, flaky 0.
findings.impact: Positive: the primary login success/failure paths and post-reload session persistence are confirmed working on the live stack. These are the journeys most likely to break a release, and they now have automated coverage.
findings.reproduction: Run `npx playwright test` from audit/artifacts/e2e against frontend :5173 / backend :8084 with admin/Admin@12345 seeded. Tests at audit.spec.ts:38, 45, 63.
findings.resolution: No fix needed. Keep these as smoke tests in CI. Consider asserting on the .login-error TEXT (not just visibility) so a future error-message regression is caught, and parameterizing credentials via env so the secret is not hard-coded in the spec.

findings.title: Access token (full JWT with roles) stored in JS-readable sessionStorage — confirmed by E2E artifact
findings.category: Session Management / Token Storage (CWE-522, CWE-1004 analog)
findings.cvss: CVSS ~5.4 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N) — a single XSS or malicious dependency can read the bearer token and impersonate the user for the token lifetime
findings.description: The login-success test reads the access token directly from sessionStorage via page.evaluate(sessionStorage.getItem('grc.accessToken') || sessionStorage.getItem('accessToken') || keys.join(',')) and writes it to session-keys.txt. The artifact contains a complete, decodable JWT. The header is {"alg":"HS384"}; the payload carries sub:1, usr:admin, org:1, a full roles array (incl. ROLE_PLATFORM_ADMIN, CYBER_WRITE/DELETE, SCM_WRITE/DELETE, EVIDENCE_WRITE/DELETE), enabled_modules, iat and exp. Because the token lives in sessionStorage it is readable by any JavaScript running in the page (XSS, malicious npm dependency, browser extension). This matches CLAUDE.md's documented design ('access token ... stored in sessionStorage') and is corroborated dynamically here. Refresh is in an HttpOnly cookie (good), but the access token itself is exposed.
findings.rootCause: Architectural choice to keep the bearer access token in Web Storage (sessionStorage) so api.js can attach Authorization: Bearer headers. Web Storage has no HttpOnly equivalent, so any script in the origin can exfiltrate it.
findings.evidence: session-keys.txt holds a raw JWT 'eyJhbGciOiJIUzM4NCJ9.<payload>.<sig>'. Decoded header: {"alg":"HS384"}. Decoded payload includes: roles=[CYBER_READ,SCM_READ,SCM_DELETE,EVIDENCE_WRITE,SCM_WRITE,EVIDENCE_DELETE,CYBER_DELETE,EVIDENCE_READ,ROLE_PLATFORM_ADMIN,CYBER_WRITE], org=1, exp=1781793757. The test wrote a token value (not just key names), proving getItem returned the JWT from sessionStorage.
findings.impact: Any XSS, compromised third-party script, or malicious browser extension on the app origin can read the full bearer token and replay it against :8084 as the authenticated user (here, a platform admin) until exp. The token also leaks the role/module entitlement model to the client. Severity capped at Medium because exploitation still requires script execution in the origin (no independent XSS confirmed by this artifact).
findings.reproduction: 1) Log in as admin on :5173. 2) Open DevTools console and run sessionStorage.getItem('grc.accessToken'). 3) Observe the full JWT is returned and base64url-decodes to the claims above. Equivalent to audit.spec.ts:41-42 / session-keys.txt.
findings.resolution: Prefer keeping the access token in memory (a module-scoped variable, never persisted) and relying on the existing HttpOnly refresh cookie + silent refresh to survive reloads, instead of persisting the access token to sessionStorage. If Web Storage must be used, add a strict Content-Security-Policy to shrink the XSS surface, keep access-token TTL short (prod is already 15m), and bind tokens where feasible. Treat session-keys.txt as a secret artifact and exclude it from any shared/committed report bundle.

findings.title: No E2E coverage for logout / session termination
findings.cvss: N/A (coverage gap) — the entire logout / session-invalidation path is unverified by any automated journey
findings.description: The suite covers login success, login failure, route-guard bypass attempt, session-on-reload, a11y and responsive screenshots, but there is NO test that logs out and verifies the session is actually terminated: that the access token is cleared from sessionStorage, that the HttpOnly refresh cookie is invalidated server-side, and that subsequently navigating back to a protected route (or hitting Back) bounces to /login. Given that the access token is held in sessionStorage (see E2E-003) and refresh in an HttpOnly cookie, logout correctness is security-relevant and currently unverified end-to-end.
findings.rootCause: Suite was scoped to login + a11y/screenshot smoke tests; the destructive/lifecycle half of the auth flow (logout, refresh-token revocation, back-button after logout) was never authored.
findings.evidence: playwright.log lists exactly 6 tests (login success, login failure, demo-skip, reload, a11y, responsive) — none reference logout. Grep of audit.spec.ts shows no 'logout', 'signout', or refresh-revocation step; the spec ends at line 121.
findings.impact: A regression that fails to clear the sessionStorage token, fails to revoke the refresh cookie, or lets the Back button restore an authenticated view after logout would ship undetected. For a multi-tenant GRC platform this is a real session-fixation / shared-device risk.
findings.reproduction: Review audit.spec.ts — no logout test exists. Manually: log in, log out, press Back / re-navigate to /risk; today nothing asserts you are bounced to /login.
findings.resolution: Add an E2E that logs in, triggers logout, then asserts: (a) sessionStorage no longer holds the access token, (b) the refresh cookie is cleared/rejected (a subsequent /api/auth/refresh returns 401), and (c) navigating to /risk lands on /login.
findings.patchBefore: // no logout test exists in audit.spec.ts

findings.title: No E2E coverage for CRUD or multi-step workflow journeys (create -> approve -> archive)
findings.category: Test Coverage Gap — Business Workflows / State Machines
findings.cvss: N/A (coverage gap) — the documented module state machines have zero end-to-end verification despite being the platform's core value
findings.description: The only interaction with the module pages (/risk, /compliance, /cyber, /privacy, /tprm, /bcm, etc.) is page.goto + screenshot + axe scan. There is NO journey that creates a record, transitions it through its documented workflow_status state machine (e.g. cyber incident DETECTION -> ... -> LESSONS_LEARNED, or a risk/compliance create -> submit -> approve -> archive), and verifies the resulting state and persistence. The workflows are the heart of a GRC product; state-transition guards live in the service layer (per CLAUDE.md) and are exactly the logic most likely to regress, yet nothing exercises them through the UI + API together.
findings.rootCause: The E2E suite was built as a login + visual/a11y smoke harness. Authoring data-mutating, multi-step workflow journeys (and the fixtures/teardown they need) was out of scope for this pass.
findings.evidence: audit.spec.ts iterates AUTH_PAGES (lines 10-20) only to goto+screenshot+axe (lines 86-97); the loop body contains no .fill on a record form, no submit of a create, and no assertion on workflow_status or row presence. playwright.log shows the AUTH_PAGES work folded into one test: 'a11y + screenshots across key pages (47.1s)'.
findings.impact: A broken state transition (e.g. an incident that can be archived while skipping approval, or a risk that loses its workflow_status on save) would not be caught. For an auditable compliance platform, undetected workflow-integrity regressions are high-business-impact.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the AUTH_PAGES loop in audit.spec.ts: it never mutates data. No create/approve/archive assertion exists anywhere in the spec.
findings.resolution: Add at least one full lifecycle journey per high-value module (start with risk and cyber-incident). Drive the real UI: create a record, advance it through each allowed transition, and assert both the rendered state and the persisted state (via an API read). Use a dedicated throwaway tenant/fixture and clean up in afterEach.

findings.title: No negative / permission-denied E2E (403 / hidden-action) journeys
findings.cvss: N/A (coverage gap) — method-level @PreAuthorize and UI gating are unverified end-to-end; a privilege-escalation regression would ship silently
findings.description: Every journey authenticates as admin (PLATFORM_ADMIN with a broad roles array — confirmed in the decoded JWT in session-keys.txt) and only exercises allowed actions. There is no test that logs in as a lower-privileged seeded role (riskmanager / Risk@12345, auditor / Audit@12345) and asserts that a forbidden action is blocked: that the API returns 403 for an action the role lacks (e.g. an AUDITOR attempting CYBER:WRITE) and that the corresponding UI control is hidden/disabled. The backend relies on @PreAuthorize(hasPermission('MODULE','ACTION')) via ModulePermissionEvaluator (per CLAUDE.md); none of that authorization surface is exercised end-to-end.
findings.rootCause: doLogin() is hard-coded to the admin superuser (audit.spec.ts:24-30), so the suite can only ever observe the permit path. No per-role fixtures exist.
findings.evidence: audit.spec.ts:24-30 doLogin always fills 'admin'/'Admin@12345'. session-keys.txt decodes to roles including ROLE_PLATFORM_ADMIN + CYBER_WRITE/DELETE + SCM_WRITE/DELETE + EVIDENCE_WRITE/DELETE — the most-privileged principal, so no denial is ever observable. No 'expect(...).toBe(403)' or 'toBeHidden' on a gated control appears in the spec.
findings.impact: A broken-access-control regression (a missing @PreAuthorize, an over-broad role grant, or a UI control that should be hidden but is not) would pass CI undetected. Broken access control is OWASP A01 and directly relevant to a multi-tenant GRC tool.
findings.reproduction: Review doLogin (audit.spec.ts:24-30) — only admin is used. No lower-privilege login or 403 assertion exists.
findings.resolution: Add per-role login helpers and at least one negative journey per sensitive action: log in as auditor (read-only), assert a write control is absent/disabled in the UI, and assert the corresponding API call returns 403. Repeat for riskmanager attempting an admin-only action.

findings.title: No cross-tenant isolation E2E (multi-tenant data-leak regressions unverified)
findings.category: Test Coverage Gap — Multi-Tenancy / Tenant Isolation (CWE-639 analog)
findings.cvss: N/A (coverage gap) — the per-query organisation_id filter (the core tenancy control) has no end-to-end verification
findings.description: The decoded session JWT carries org:1, meaning every journey runs entirely inside tenant org_id=1 (TSS GRC). CLAUDE.md documents that there is NO global Hibernate tenant filter — every repository query must hand-filter by organisation_id, making this an error-prone, per-query control. The seed data sets up three tenants (org_id 1, 2, 3: TSS GRC, Aramco Trading, STC Bank). Nothing in the suite logs in under two different tenants and asserts that tenant A cannot read tenant B's records (neither via the UI nor by directly requesting another tenant's resource id from tenant A's session). Tenant isolation is therefore completely unverified end-to-end.
findings.rootCause: Single-tenant test fixture (admin in org 1 only) and no second-tenant credential, so a cross-tenant read can never be attempted, let alone asserted to fail.
findings.evidence: session-keys.txt JWT payload: 'org':'1'. CLAUDE.md: 'Every repository query must filter by organisation_id ... There is no global Hibernate filter for this; it is the developer's responsibility per query.' seed_real_data.py documents tenants org_id 1/2/3. The spec has no second-tenant login and no cross-tenant fetch assertion.
findings.impact: A single repository method that forgets its findBy...OrganisationId filter would leak another tenant's GRC data (risks, incidents, evidence). For a multi-tenant compliance platform this is among the highest-impact failure modes, and it is invisible to the current suite.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the suite — only org_id=1 (admin) is ever authenticated. No tenant-B principal or cross-tenant resource fetch exists.
findings.resolution: Seed a user in a second tenant (org_id=2). Add an E2E that: as tenant A, creates/locates a record and notes its id; as tenant B, attempts to GET that id and asserts 403/404 (not 200 with the row); and asserts tenant B's list views never contain tenant A's records. This must be re-run whenever a repository finder changes.
findings.patchBefore: // every test runs as admin in org_id=1 only; no second tenant is ever authenticated

findings.title: Recommended Playwright suite structure to close the verified E2E coverage gaps
findings.cvss: N/A (recommendation) — proposes the file/fixture layout that would land E2E-004 through E2E-007
findings.description: The current single-file audit.spec.ts mixes auth smoke, a11y, and responsive screenshots and has no role/tenant fixtures, no API-level assertions, and no data cleanup. To close gaps E2E-004 (logout), E2E-005 (workflow lifecycle), E2E-006 (permission-denied) and E2E-007 (tenant isolation), split into per-concern specs backed by shared auth fixtures (one storageState per seeded role/tenant) so journeys are fast and isolated, and add API assertions alongside DOM assertions so persisted state — not just rendered state — is verified.
findings.rootCause: Audit harness was intentionally minimal (one smoke file). Production-grade coverage needs fixtures, projects, and teardown that the current single spec lacks.
findings.evidence: audit.spec.ts is a single 121-line file with all six tests; report.json shows one project, workers:1, no globalSetup/globalTeardown (config lines 13-14). No fixtures or storageState are used.
findings.impact: Adopting the skeleton makes role- and tenant-scoped journeys cheap to add and keeps the security-relevant gaps (logout, authz, isolation, workflow integrity) under continuous verification.
findings.reproduction: N/A — structural recommendation derived from the existing spec/config.
findings.resolution: Introduce a fixtures module that produces authenticated contexts per role/tenant via storageState, a global setup that logs each principal in once, and per-domain spec files. Keep the existing a11y/responsive specs as-is.
findings.patchBefore: // tests/audit.spec.ts  (single file: login smoke + a11y + responsive, admin-only, no fixtures)
